My academic path connects physics, machine learning, and bioinformatics. Research gives me a space to explore open questions in biomolecular modeling, while teaching helps me revisit foundational ideas and communicate them with clarity.

## Current Appointments

::: {.timeline}
::: {.timeline-item}
### CONICET Doctoral Fellow

**2025–present**

My doctoral work explores predictive and generative modeling of RNA secondary structure, supervised by Prof. Diego H. Milone and Dr. Leandro Bugnon. My day-to-day work combines model development, data analysis, reproducible experiments, and the interpretation of results across computational and biological perspectives.
:::

::: {.timeline-item}
### Teaching Assistant

**Facultad de Ingeniería y Ciencias Hídricas, Universidad Nacional del Litoral · 2026–present**

I teach Neural Networks I and Neural Networks II as an *Ayudante de Primera* in the [Ingeniería en Inteligencia Artificial](https://www.unl.edu.ar/carreras/ingenieria-en-inteligencia-artificial/) program. I aim to help students connect mathematical concepts with implementation decisions and develop an informed, practical understanding of how neural models behave.
:::

:::

## Education

**PhD in Engineering – Computational Intelligence**, Universidad Nacional del Litoral, 2025–present<br>
Thesis topic: generative models for joint sequence-structure representations and RNA ensembles.

**Licentiate Degree in Physics**, Universidad Nacional de Rosario, 2016–2024<br>
Thesis on machine-learning simulations of dissociative adsorption of methane on Pt(110)-(1×2).

My training in physics shaped the way I approach computational problems: by looking for interpretable models, carefully defined assumptions, and connections between numerical results and the systems they describe.

## Previous Research

**Instituto de Física Rosario (IFIR), UNR-CONICET · 2022–2024**<br>
As an EVC-CIN undergraduate research fellow, I worked on neural-network interatomic potentials and computational simulations of methane adsorption on platinum surfaces. This experience introduced me to data-driven scientific modeling and provided the foundation for my later work at the intersection of machine learning and molecular systems.

## Selected Presentations

These presentations reflect the transition from my early work in computational surface physics to my current focus on RNA structure and bioinformatics.

**I Jornada Argentina de Bioinformática y Biología Computacional · 2025**<br>
Poster: “Enhancing Deep Learning Prediction of Base-Pairing Probability in RNA Sequences Using Structural Diversity.”

**X Encuentro de Física y Química de Superficies, CNEA · 2024**<br>
Poster: “Dissociative Adsorption of Methane on Pt(110)-(1×2) Using Machine Learning.”
